items.text: Global estimates published in The Lancet reveal that over a billion people worldwide are living with obesity, with approximately 880 million adults and 159 million children affected. Tonga and American Samoa show the highest rates for both men and women. The UK ranks 55th for men and 87th for women out of 200 countries. Experts emphasize the urgent need for significant changes in addressing obesity. The World Health Organization stresses the importance of government and food industry support to combat obesity, especially among youth. Obesity rates have doubled in the UK over the last three decades, alarming researchers. The study underscores the rapid rise in obesity levels since 1990, urging governments to prioritize this health issue associated with various ailments like heart disease, diabetes, and cancer. Difficult words: underscore (to emphasize), prioritize (to treat something as being very or most important), ailment (a health problem or disease). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A recent study shows that over a billion people worldwide are obese . It is a growing trend. 880 million adults and 159 million children live with obesity . Tonga and American Samoa have the highest rates, and 70-80% of adults have this problem. In the UK, obesity rates doubled in the last 30 years. The World Health Organization urges governments and the food industry to help fight obesity, especially among young people. The World Health Organization asked governments and food companies to act quickly. The authors of the study said that they were shocked by the rapid rise in obesity since 1990. Difficult words: obese (very fat), obesity (when someone is very fat), urge (to press someone to do something), rapid (fast). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A study finds a big problem. More than a billion people are too fat. This includes 159 million children and 880 million adults . Places like Tonga and American Samoa have lots of fat people. More than 70%. Even in the UK, many adults have this problem. There are two times more fat people than 30 years ago. The World Health Organization says that this is serious . They ask leaders and food companies to help people eat better and move more. More children are getting fat too. It is important to do something with it quickly. Difficult words: include (to have something as a part of something else), adult (a person who is not a child anymore), serious (bad and important). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US President Donald Trump reported over 1.4 billion dollars in income from his family’s cryptocurrency ventures in 2025, according to his latest financial disclosure. Digital assets now provide the majority of his income, as he benefits heavily from his administration’s crypto-friendly policies. Trump’s company received nearly 800 million from a project co-founded with his sons. This total includes 520 million dollars from token sales and 250 million from selling business interests. Additionally, sales of the Trump memecoin generated 635 million, and marked a massive increase from the 57 million reported the previous year. Since his 2025 inauguration, the Trump family has earned an estimated 2.3 billion from digital currencies. While a White House spokesperson denied any conflicts of interest, Trump’s traditional businesses also thrived. His golf courses and resorts brought in over 500 million, and showed the strongest growth at clubs where the president spends significant time. Difficult words: venture (a new business activity, project, or plan that involves taking risks to make money), disclosure (an official document or statement that makes new or secret financial information public), token (a unit of digital currency used on a specific crypto platform or project). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

US President Donald Trump made more than 1.4 billion dollars from digital currency projects in 2025. A new official financial report shows that most of his income now comes from these digital assets . Trump and his sons started a crypto project called World Liberty Financial, which earned nearly 800 million. This money came from selling digital tokens and business shares . Trump also made 635 million from a special digital coin named after him. Since he returned to the White House, his family earned around 2.3 billion from digital money. A spokesperson said there is no problem with his official work and business. At the same time, Trump’s businesses, like his golf clubs and beautiful resorts, did very well and brought in more than 500 million last year. Difficult words: asset (something valuable a person or a company owns), token (a unit of digital currency), share (one of many parts of a company which you can buy or sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump is the president of the United States. He makes more than 1.4 billion dollars from digital money in 2025. A new financial report shows that digital assets are now his biggest source of money. Trump and his sons have a business called World Liberty Financial. They sell digital coins . They make hundreds of millions of dollars. In 2025, Trump becomes president again. His family makes billions of dollars from this business. A White House worker says that everything is legal and fair. Trump has other businesses, too. He has golf clubs and hotels. They bring him over 500 million dollars last year. Difficult words: asset (something a person or company has, for example, a house, land, or money), source (where something comes from), coin (a metal piece of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Plastic period products rank as the fifth most common single-use plastic item found on European beaches, surpassing plastic cups and straws, according to the European Parliament. Efforts to tackle this issue include developing biopolymer -based alternatives, derived from algae, which are naturally white or colorless, eliminating the need for bleaching. These biopolymer fibers are used to create tampons, similar to those made from cotton or viscose . While such alternatives absorb carbon, their climate neutrality depends on cultivation methods. Researchers and companies are exploring technologies for sustainable cultivation, both on land and in the sea, to produce these biodegradable hygiene products, offering a promising solution to reduce waste. Difficult words: biopolymer (a polymer produced by living organisms), viscose (a smooth material similar to silk but made from cellulose), cultivation (growing or nurturing something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Plastic period products are very bad for the natural world. They are fifth among single-use plastics on European beaches, which is even higher than plastic cups and straws. The European Parliament said that it was necessary to look for alternatives . One such alternative involves biopolymer fibers which come from algae. It is naturally white or colorless, therefore it is not necessary to bleach it. These fibers are used to make tampons, but their climate impact depends on how farmers grow algae. More companies are looking for a solution which will be more friendly to the natural world but safe for women to use. Difficult words: single-use (something what you use only once), alternative (a different option), biopolymer (a polymer which comes from living organisms), bleach (to make something white). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Plastic period products are bad for the natural world. They are the fifth most common plastic on European beaches. There are more of them than plastic cups and straws. The European Parliament wants to find better options . They are looking into using biodegradable materials, like fibers from algae, to make tampons. These tampons are from a white material. So it is not necessary to make them white with chemicals. It is important to grow these materials in a way which does not hurt the natural world. Researchers are working on better ways to do this on land and in the sea. We need to throw away less plastics. Difficult words: period (a flow of blood from a woman’s body which happens every month), option (a thing you may choose), biodegradable (able to break down naturally). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brazil is taking a high-tech approach to stop illegal gold mining in the Amazon. Scientists use forensic methods to trace the ‘DNA of Brazilian gold’. They use advanced tools to detect the unique impurities , tiny bits of other materials like dirt or copper, that reveal their origin. Illegal gold mining has grown under weakened regulations during the Bolsonaro administration and now accounts for nearly half of Brazil’s gold output. This mining causes environmental destruction and violence in the Amazon. Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has promised to crack down on these activities, aided by the ‘Targeting Gold’ program. The program, developed with universities, has already helped police seize 38% more gold in 2023 than in 2022. Brazil’s new methods are getting attention from other countries, like Colombia and France, which want to adopt the technology. Brazilian scientists are open to collaborating globally to improve gold tracing. Difficult words: forensic (scientific methods used to investigate), impurity (a small amount of unwanted substance), aid (to help). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Brazil is using advanced science to stop illegal gold mining in the Amazon. Scientists study gold samples to figure out where they come from. They use special machines to find bits of other materials like dirt or copper, which help identify the source. Illegal gold mining accounts for nearly half of Brazil’s gold production. This mining causes harm to the environment and brings crime to the Amazon. Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, wants to fight back. He started a program which already helped police seize more gold in 2023 than in 2022. Other countries like Cambodia and France are interested in Brazil’s new methods. Brazil is also open to working with other countries to improve gold tracing . Difficult words: identify (to find out who or what someone or something is), account for (to form the total of something), seize (to take hold of something), tracing (finding where something is from). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brazil is using science to stop illegal gold mining . Scientists study gold to learn where it comes from. They use special tools to find small bits of other materials, like dirt. They show where the gold is from. Illegal gold mining is a big problem in Brazil. It harms the Amazon rainforest and brings crime . Almost half of Brazil’s gold comes from illegal mining. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva starts a program to stop it. The program helps police catch more illegal gold this year than last year. Other countries like Colombia and France want to use Brazil’s new method . Brazil says that it will help teach others how to find out where gold comes from. Difficult words: mining (getting minerals and materials from the ground), crime (illegal activity), method (the way of doing something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A powerful summer heatwave moving across Europe recently brought extreme temperatures to Germany and Hungary, while a violent nighttime thunderstorm broke the heat in Paris. During this storm, a spectacular lightning strike hit the Eiffel Tower, which was captured from multiple angles on social media. Experts explain that despite the intense storm, visitors inside the tower’s restaurants or elevators remain completely safe and feel nothing. This safety is due to a sophisticated lightning protection system originally envisioned by Gustave Eiffel in 1889. The structure features nine lightning rods connected to copper cables that safely conduct the massive electrical currents, averaging 30,000 amperes, directly into the ground. Beyond protection, the tower operates as an active scientific laboratory. Engineers constantly gather data on lightning waveforms and characteristics to study meteorology and improve components. For storm watchers, local guides recommend viewing these rare events safely from a distance, from elevated spots like Montmartre or Trocadéro. Difficult words: envision (to imagine or picture something as a clear possibility for the future when planning a project), conduct (to allow electricity, heat, or light to travel easily through a wire or a material), constantly (happening all the time, again and again, or without stopping). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A major European heatwave recently moved east toward Germany and Hungary, while a big storm brought lightning and cooler air to Paris. During the storm, lightning struck the Eiffel Tower. This happens five to ten times every year, but people inside the tower are completely safe. They cannot feel the electricity because the tower has a special protection system. Gustave Eiffel designed this system in 1889. There are nine lightning rods on the tower connected to large copper cables. These cables take the heavy electricity safely down into the ground. Today, engineers use the tower as a scientific laboratory. They collect data from sensors to study the storms and make the protection better. Experts say that the best and safest places to watch these beautiful storms are from far away, at spots like Montmartre. Difficult words: rod (a long, thin, and straight piece of wood, metal, or plastic), copper (a soft, reddish-brown metal that is very good at conducting electricity and heat), sensor (a small electronic tool that can find, measure, and record changes in light, heat, or electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big summer storm brings thunder and bright lightning to Paris. During this storm, lightning hits the Eiffel Tower. Many people see it and take beautiful photos. Visitors inside the tower are safe. They do not feel anything. Gustave Eiffel has a plan for this in 1889. The tower has nine long pieces of special metal and long copper lines. These lines take the electricity down into the ground. Today, scientists use the tower to study storms and weather. Experts say that it is beautiful to watch the lightning, but people should look from a safe place far away. Difficult words: thunder (the loud sound which you hear in the sky during a storm), lightning (a bright flash of electricity which moves in the sky between clouds or from a cloud to the ground), copper (a soft, reddish-brown metal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For most of human history, the night sky was not just for scientists; it was vital for survival. In the Australian outback , the sky shines with the Milky Way’s 100 billion stars. Aboriginal legends, like those of the Wiradjuri nation, use constellations to guide seasonal activities like collecting eggs. Polynesians were master navigators, exploring over 1,000 Pacific islands by memorizing star patterns. They used specific stars to guide their journeys, switching stars as they rose and set. Europeans also relied on celestial navigation with the sun, moon, and stars to travel the world. Ancient structures like Stonehenge and Newgrange aligned with the solstice , helping track time and organize rituals. Chankillo in Peru offered a solar calendar with its 13 towers. Today, technologies like GPS replace these methods. However, light pollution hides the stars from most people and disrupts animals like birds that navigate by them. The sky shaped human culture and guided our evolution and identity. Difficult words: vital (necessary), outback (the remote and usually uninhabited inland districts of Australia), solstice (the longest or the shortest day of the year). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For most of history, people used the night sky for survival . In Australia, the Milky Way shines brightly. Aboriginal people like the Wiradjuri watch stars to know the right time to collect food. Polynesians were skilled navigators who traveled across the Pacific by learning the movement of stars. European sailors also used the stars for navigation . Ancient sites like Stonehenge and Newgrange helped track time, especially during the winter solstice , to organize important rituals. Today, people use GPS instead of stars. Too much light at night blocks the stars for many people. Animals like birds, which rely on stars to navigate, also have problems. Still, the sky reminds us of how humans used it to find food, travel, and organize life. Difficult words: survival (continuing to live), navigation (moving around a place), solstice (the longest or shortest day of the year). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the past, people need the night sky to live. In Australia, the Milky Way lights up the night. Aboriginal people watch stars to know when to pick food. Polynesians travel the Pacific Ocean by watching the stars. European sailors also use the sky to find their way. Ancient places like Stonehenge and Newgrange help people know time. People hold ceremonies during the shortest days of the year. Today, we use GPS instead of the stars. But too much light at night makes it hard for people and animals, like birds, to see the night sky. Difficult words: aboriginal (the first people who live in a country or area), sailor (a person who has a job on a ship or boat), ancient (very old). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Global power dynamics are shifting as countries look for new ways to manage China’s rising influence and its alliance with Russia. A new proposal suggests dividing geopolitical strategy into three specialized areas. The first area focuses on sea power and coordinates allies like Japan and Australia to control nine critical ocean choke points used by Chinese ships. The second area focuses on the rimland , crucial zones like the Middle East, where land and sea powers meet, by developing massive trade networks like the India-Middle East Economic Corridor. Meanwhile, countries are building long-term plans to counter Chinese and Russian expansion on land in Eurasia. This new view is reflected in the Pentagon’s decision to rename its regional command back to Pacific Command. This change happened because leaders realized that India’s massive mountain borders effectively isolate it geopolitically and make it far less important to China’s land-based trade plans than Central Asia. Difficult words: dynamics (the way that people or countries behave and react to each other, and changes over time), choke point (a very narrow and important water path or street that can easily be blocked to stop ships or armies from passing), rimland (the outer edge or coastal areas of a huge piece of land, especially around Europe and Asia, where sea and land powers meet). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The United States and its allies need a better plan to handle global politics and China’s growth. Experts suggest using three new groups to manage different parts of the world. One group will work with sea powers like Japan to control important paths in the ocean. Another group will focus on areas like the Middle East, where land and sea powers meet, by building big trade roads to connect countries. At the same time, governments in Europe and Asia are making long-term plans to stop China and Russia from becoming too strong on land. Finally, the American military recently renamed its Pacific Command. They now see that India’s high mountains separate it from China, so India is actually less important to China’s trade plans than Central Asia. Difficult words: ally (a country or a person that helps and supports you because you have the same goals or a special agreement), path (a track, route, or way which allows you to move from one place to another), long-term (happening, continuing, or planned for a long period of time in the future, not just for today or tomorrow). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Western countries must work together because China and Russia are getting very strong. Leaders want to use three new groups to keep the world safe. The first group helps sea countries like America and Japan control important water paths in the ocean. The second group helps countries in Asia and the Middle East build big roads for business and trade. Many governments are making long-term plans to stay safe. Also, the United States changes the name of its army group in the Pacific. They see that India has very big mountains on the border , so China cannot build railways there. This means that India is not part of China’s main plans. Difficult words: path (a track or way), long-term (planned for a long time, not just for a few days), border (the official line on a map between two countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Commission has proposed extending the temporary protection scheme for Ukrainian refugees until March 2028, but with a major change: excluding military-age Ukrainian men. This new measure, backed by Kyiv and several EU member states, targets men aged 23 to 60 who cannot legally leave Ukraine due to military obligations under martial law . The decision aims to support Ukraine’s defense needs as the country faces serious shortages in its armed forces. However, the rule will not apply retroactively , which means that Ukrainian men who already hold temporary protection status in the EU will not lose it. To become law, the proposal requires approval by a qualified majority of EU countries. In a similar move, Denmark announced that military-age Ukrainian men will receive residence permits only if they can prove they are legally exempt from military service. Additionally, the Commission proposed a voluntary return program to support refugees who wish to go home. Difficult words: excluding (leaving someone or something out, or saying that a specific person or group cannot join a program), martial law (a strict rule controlled by the army instead of the normal police, used when a country is in a big danger or war), retroactively (changing how things worked in the past, or making a new rule apply to things that already happened before), exempt (having a special permission not to do a job or a duty that everyone else is legally forced to do). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The European Commission wants to change the rules for Ukrainian refugees . They plan to continue the special protection program until March 2028. But new Ukrainian men aged 23 to 60 will not get this protection if they must serve in the military. Kyiv and some EU countries support this plan because Ukraine needs more soldiers to defend the country. This new rule is only for future refugees; men who already have protection in the EU will keep their documents and can stay. For this plan to start, a large majority of EU countries must vote for it. At the same time, Denmark is making a similar rule, and the EU is also planning a program to help refugees who want to return home. Difficult words: refugee (a person who must run away from their home country because it is dangerous there due to war or a disaster), protection (the state of being kept safe from danger, bad weather, war, or anything that can hurt you), majority (a number or a group of people that is more than half of the total number of people in a room or a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Union has a big new plan for refugees from Ukraine. The EU wants to help these families and protect them until March 2028. But there is a new rule for men between 23 and 60 years old. If these men must be soldiers in Ukraine, the EU will not give them new protection documents. Ukraine needs more soldiers, so leaders agree with this change. Men who already live in the EU with protection are safe. They can stay. Many EU countries must now vote on this plan. Denmark is also doing the same thing. Difficult words: refugee (a person who must run away from their home country because it is not safe there), protect (to keep safe), protection (when somebody stays away from a dangerous situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An exceptional June heatwave has shattered temperature records across Europe and affected at least 150 million people with temperatures exceeding 35 degrees Celsius. Germany recorded its highest temperature ever at 41.3 degrees in Saarbrücken, while cities like Bordeaux experienced their hottest days on record. The extreme weather has forced French authorities to cancel major public events, including music festivals and Paris Pride, and limit public alcohol consumption due to severe health risks. In the Netherlands, the weather service issued its first-ever red alert as intense heat partially suspended public transport because electric buses couldn’t charge. Meteorologists explain that a massive heat dome, an area of high pressure, is trapping and compressing hot air coming from the south, and that prevents temperatures from dropping even at night. While western areas are beginning to cool down slightly, the dangerous high-pressure system is currently sweeping further east toward Switzerland, Austria, Poland, and Hungary. Difficult words: shatter (to beat or break an old record by a very big margin), red alert (the highest level of an official warning), suspend (to stop an activity, service, or law officially for a short period of time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A very dangerous heatwave is hitting Europe right now, and June temperature records are breaking in many countries. In Germany, the weather service recorded a historic temperature of over 41 degrees Celsius. Because of the extreme heat, France had to cancel big summer festivals and street parties to protect people’s health. In the Netherlands, officials issued a red alert for the first time because electric buses couldn’t charge, which stopped public transport. Weather experts say that a big area of high pressure is acting like a heat dome. This dome traps the hot air and warm sunshine, so the land can’t cool down during the night. The hot weather is now moving from western Europe toward eastern countries like Poland, Austria, and Hungary. Difficult words: historic (something that happens for the very first time), red alert (the highest level of an official warning), pressure (the weight of the air pushing down on the earth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe is very hot right now. Many countries are breaking old summer records . Germany has a historic day with over 41 degrees Celsius. This hot weather is dangerous for people. In France, officials stop big music parties on the streets because of the heat. In the Netherlands, big electric buses do not work, so people can not travel. Weather experts say that hot air from the south stays under a big dome . The hot air cannot go away, so even the nights are very warm. Now, this hot weather is moving to more countries in the east. Difficult words: record (the best, highest, or lowest number or result ever), historic (something what happens for the first time), dome (a round shape like the top half of a ball or a large bowl turned upside down). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ozempic, originally developed in 2017 to treat type 2 diabetes, has rapidly transformed into a massive cultural phenomenon due to its weight-loss effects. Driven by aggressive advertising campaigns that cost over half a billion dollars annually, advertisements for these injections have become completely pervasive in the United States. Media platforms frequently broadcast before and after videos that show larger bodies in purely negative, depressing terms, which further stigmatize weight issues. This exposure creates intense social pressure across all age groups and genders to pursue extreme thinness, reminiscent of the diet culture of the 1990s. Scientific research warns that this damages body image and drives individuals toward risky behaviors, including disordered eating and illegal online purchases by people who don’t qualify medically. Even peak professional athletes like Serena Williams have become commercial ambassadors for these wellness platforms. Experts warn that marketing is overshadowing scientific caution and the potential side effects of these powerful drugs. Difficult words: phenomenon (a big, surprising, or extremely popular event in society that everyone is suddenly talking about and watching), pervasive (present or noticeable everywhere around you, so it is almost impossible to escape or avoid it), stigmatize (to make a person or a group feel ashamed or left out because of their appearance, weight, or situation), reminiscent (making you remember or think about something similar that happened in the past). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At first, Ozempic helped people with diabetes, but it is now famous all over the world for helping people lose weight. The companies which make these injections spend hundreds of millions of dollars on television advertisements . Today, almost every adult in the United States sees these ads every week. The advertisements always show thin people who look very happy, which puts a lot of pressure on normal people to change their bodies immediately. This pressure is dangerous because it makes people feel bad about their weight, and some even stop eating healthy food or buy the drug illegally on the internet. Even famous sports stars get to sell these products, for example, Serena Williams. Scientists say we must be very careful because the media talks about a miracle drug, but people forget about the dangerous medical risks. Difficult words: advertisement (a video, picture, or text on TV or the internet meant to persuade people to buy a product), pressure (a strong feeling that you must do something because other people, society, or your friends expect it from you), miracle (an amazing, wonderful, and almost impossible event that people cannot explain, or something that works perfectly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ozempic is now very famous in America. First, it helps sick people, but now many people use it to look thin. The companies spend a lot of money on big television advertisements . Normal parents and children see these advertisements every week. The videos show that thin people are always happy and big people are sad. This makes everyone want to lose weight . It makes people feel bad about their bodies. Some people even buy the medicine online without a doctor’s prescription. Scientists say that this is dangerous. We must follow the rules of science, not television. We must speak about the risks of Ozempic, too. Difficult words: advertisement (a video, picture, or text on TV or the internet which makes people want to buy a product), weight (how heavy a person or an object is), ri sk (the chance of something bad happening to your health or life). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Commission is set to escalate its official investigation into Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram. According to recent reports, EU regulators are preparing preliminary findings that accuse the tech giant of using addictive design practices specifically to keep children hooked on its social media platforms. This move follows previous charges from April, where the EU accused Meta of breaching tech rules and failing to block children under 13 from accessing its networks. The commission is now considering strict new restrictions next month after receiving recommendations from an expert panel. Meanwhile, Meta is facing massive legal pressure globally. In the US, the company is lobbying Congress for legal immunity against claims of harming children, especially after a landmark court verdict found both Meta and Google negligent in designing platforms harmful to youth. Difficult words: preliminary (coming before the main or final part of something, like the first quick results of a big test), hooked (unable to stop doing or using something because you like it too much and are addicted to it), lobby (to try very hard to talk to and persuade politicians to change a law to help your company), negligent (failing to take enough care of something you are responsible for, which then causes harm to others). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Leaders in the European Union are increasing their investigation into Meta, the big company that owns Facebook and Instagram. Important officials say that Meta designs its apps to be addictive to children. The government says the company broke tech rules because it doesn’t stop children under 13 years old from using these social networks. Next month, a special group of experts will give advice, and the EU might make new rules to protect young people. Meta is also having big legal problems in the United States. Many families are taking the company to court because their children were hurt by social media. Meta is trying to influence American politicians so it doesn’t have to pay for these problems. Difficult words: investigation (the official process of finding out all the facts about a crime, a problem, or a company), addictive (making you want to do or have something so much that you cannot stop, even if it is bad for you), influence (to have the power to change how someone thinks, behaves, or makes their decisions). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European leaders are looking into a big computer company called Meta. This company owns Facebook and Instagram. The leaders say that the company makes its apps dangerous for children. They think that the apps make children look at screens too much. The company also lets children under 13 use the networks, and this is against the EU rules. Next month, some experts will help make new rules to keep young people safe. In the United States, many parents are angry because these apps hurt their children. Many people are taking the company to court . But the company is asking politicians for help to stop the parents. Difficult words: own (when something belongs to you, it is yours), dangerous (not safe), court (the official place where people decide if someone breaks the law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Archaeologists have discovered a much simpler, earlier version of Stonehenge just five kilometers away from the famous prehistoric monument. This ancient structure is about 5,000 years old, which predates Stonehenge by 500 years. All that remains of this older site are two large holes in the ground separated by 120 meters. Experts confirm that these pits once held massive wooden posts that lined up perfectly with the rising sun on the summer solstice and the setting sun on the winter solstice. The wooden posts themselves have long since rotted away, and the site is now located beneath a modern housing estate. During excavations , scientists found various ancient artefacts, including delicate pottery, flint tools, and animal bones. These discoveries suggest that prehistoric farming communities gathered there to celebrate the changing seasons. For the lead archaeologist, this breakthrough provides incredible insights into how early human communities behaved and viewed the heavens. Difficult words: predate (to be older than something else, or to happen at an earlier time in history), pit (a big, deep hole dug into the ground to hold a large wooden pole or post upright), excavation (the careful digging in the ground by scientists to find hidden things from the past), flint (a very hard, grey stone that ancient people used as a tool to cut things or make fire). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists found an older and simpler version of Stonehenge just five kilometers away from the famous monument. This new site is 5,000 years old, which means it is 500 years older than Stonehenge. Today, only two big holes are left in the ground. Archaeologists say these holes held tall wooden posts a long time ago. The wood is gone now, but scientists proved that the posts lined up perfectly with the sun during the longest and shortest days of the year. Workers also found ancient objects at the site, such as beautiful pots, stone tools, and animal bones. These things show that early farmers gathered there to celebrate the seasons. The discovery is very exciting because it helps us understand how these ancient people lived, worked, and looked at the sky. Difficult words: version (a form of something a little different from other forms of the same thing), prove (to show that something is true by using facts, science, or information), ancient (from thousands of years ago). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists find a very old place near the famous Stonehenge. This place is 5,000 years old. It is 500 years older than Stonehenge. Now, there are only two big holes in the ground. A long time ago, these holes have tall pieces of wood inside them. The wood is not there now, but the lines face the sun on the longest and shortest days of the year. Scientists also find old things there, like pots, stone tools, and animal bones . These things show that early people came together at this place. It helps us see the lives of families and children a long time ago. Difficult words: hole (a space in the ground), wood (the hard substance which comes from trees), bone (the hard white parts inside an animal or person).

Japan is currently facing a severe loneliness crisis, driven by its rapidly aging population and shrinking family sizes. Nearly 30% of Japanese citizens are aged 65 or older, which makes it the oldest population in the world. Last year, nearly 77,000 people died completely alone in their homes, a tragic situation known locally as kodokushi (lonely death). To help isolated seniors, local support networks have formed, such as delivery workers who check on elderly residents during daily yogurt deliveries. However, this crisis doesn’t just affect the elderly. Younger generations also face extreme social isolation due to intense work pressure and emotional disconnection. The problem became so widespread that the government created a Minister of Loneliness in 2021. Today, a billion-dollar industry has emerged. It offers paid conversation partners and hotlines to help lonely people buy basic human company on demand to combat their isolation. Difficult words: rapidly (very quickly), isolated (completely alone, separated from other people, and far away from friends or family), combat (to fight against something bad or try very hard to stop a dangerous problem from getting worse). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Japan has a problem with loneliness because it has the world’s oldest population. Almost 30% of the people are over 65 years old. Many old people live alone because their children move far away for work. Last year, nearly 77,000 people died alone in their houses, and nobody found them for days or months. Now, some companies help them; for example, yogurt delivery workers talk to old people every morning to check if they are healthy. But young people are also lonely because they have too much pressure at work. The government even made a special Minister of Loneliness to fix this problem. Lonely people can now use phone apps to buy a conversation partner to have someone to talk to. Difficult words: loneliness (the unhappy feeling you have because you are alone and do not have any friends or people to talk to), pressure (a stressful and difficult feeling when you have too much hard work or when people expect too much from you), lonely (sad because you are without anyone around). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people in Japan are very lonely . Japan has many old people. It is the oldest population in the world. Many old people live alone because their children live far away. Last year, many thousands of people die alone in their homes. Now, some good workers visit old people every morning to give them food and talk to them. But young people are lonely too because they work too much. Since 2021, Japan has a special minister to help lonely people. Now, people can use phone apps. They pay to talk to a person because they want a friend. Difficult words: lonely (sad because there is nobody to be with you or talk to you), population (the number of people who live in a town or country), minister (an important leader who cares about a specific thing in a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bowel cancer cases among adults under 50 are rising globally, though the exact reasons remain unclear. While the disease still affects mostly older people, experts are concerned about this younger group. England has seen one of the largest increases, with a yearly rise of 3.6%. Researchers believe poor diets, obesity, and lack of exercise may contribute to this trend. Factors like improved early detection and genetic changes might also play a role. Symptoms like changes in bowel habits, unexplained weight loss, or fatigue should prompt a doctor’s visit. Early diagnosis is crucial, as it significantly improves treatment outcomes. Dr. Rachel Orritt from Cancer Research UK highlights the importance of studying the causes to develop prevention strategies. A team funded by Cancer Research UK is investigating these factors globally. Despite the rise, bowel cancer remains rare in younger adults, with only about 1 in 20 cases occurring in this group. Difficult words: detection (finding something early), prevention (the action of stopping something from happening or arising). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Bowel cancer cases in people under 50 are going up in many countries. England has one of the highest increases, with 3.6% more cases every year. Poor diet, obesity, and not enough exercise might cause this rise, but experts are not sure yet. Better testing and genetic factors may also be part of the problem. Cancer Research UK is studying why younger people are getting bowel cancer more often. They are also finding ways to stop it. While bowel cancer is still rare in young adults, it is important to see a doctor early if you notice symptoms . These include changes in bowel habits, weight loss, or feeling very tired. Early treatment gives the best chance to recover. Difficult words: bowel (the long tube that carries waste from the stomach out of the body), rare (not common, or very usual), symptom (a sign of illness). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bowel cancer is more usual in older people. But it is growing in younger adults under 50. In England, cases are going up by 3.6% every year. Experts think that this happens because of bad food, being overweight , and not moving enough. They are still studying why this is happening. Better testing and genetics can be part of the problem, too. If you feel unwell, it is good to see a doctor early. You may feel different when you go to the toilet. You may get slim without trying. You may be very tired. If doctors catch cancer early, they can help you stop it. Difficult words: bowel (the long tube through which food travels from the stomach out of the body), case (when something happens), overweight (fat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brussels will completely ban shared e-scooters from its streets starting January 2027 due to growing safety concerns. The Belgian capital joins other major European cities like Paris, Madrid, and Prague that have already outlawed them. The local government decided not to renew the licences of the operators, Bolt and Dott, after a 26% increase in accidents in 2025 left 666 people injured. Medical experts warn that e-scooter crashes often cause severe head and facial injuries. Additionally, poorly parked scooters frequently clutter pavements, obstruct public ways and create serious difficulties for the elderly and people with reduced mobility. Surprisingly, authorities also revealed a strong link to organized crime. They said drug traffickers used e-scooters in 25 shootings last year. While rental e-scooters will disappear completely, Brussels plans to strengthen its transportation network by expanding the availability of shared bicycles and e-bikes instead. Difficult words: outlaw (to make something completely illegal or forbid it by an official government law), clutter (to fill a space with too many messy things so that it looks untidy and is difficult to use), trafficker (a criminal who buys and sells illegal goods, like dangerous drugs or weapons). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Brussels will ban all rental e-scooters from its streets in January 2027. The capital of Belgium is following other big European cities like Paris, Madrid, and Prague, which already stopped them. Local leaders made this decision because accidents increased by 26% in one year, and hurt over 600 people. Doctors say that e-scooter accidents often cause bad head injuries. Also, people leave the scooters in bad places on the pavements . This blocks the way and makes walking dangerous for old people and people who cannot move easily. The government also said that dangerous criminal groups and drug sellers use these scooters to commit crimes. Instead of e-scooters, Brussels will give more money to its bike-sharing system and put more regular and electric bicycles on the streets. Difficult words: rental (something that you pay money to use instead of buying it), pavement (a path next to a road for people to walk on), commit (to do something illegal, bad, or wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brussels will stop all rental e-scooters in January 2027. Other big cities like Madrid, Paris, and Prague already stop them too. Leaders say that the small electric vehicles are dangerous. Many people hurt their heads in bad accidents on them. Also, people park them in bad places on the streets. This makes walking very difficult for old people and children. The government also says that bad people use the scooters to do crimes. Brussels wants the streets to be safe for everyone. So, the city will put many more regular and electric bicycles on the roads for people to use instead . Difficult words: rental (when you pay to use something rather than buying the thing), regular (normal, usual), instead (in the place of something else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

About 14% of US households earn over 200,000 dollars annually, but many high earners don’t feel rich. These individuals are called HENRYs—High Earners, Not Rich Yet. Even people making over 300,000 often struggle with credit card debt. This is partly due to lifestyle creep , where people increase their spending as their income rises. Many HENRYs live in high-cost cities and have growing expenses like rent, food delivery, and subscriptions. They compare themselves to others in their income group, making them feel financially behind. Experts say budgeting, knowing your net worth , and planning for savings are key steps to feeling financially secure. While earning more can offer freedom, it doesn’t always reduce stress. Emotional spending, social pressure, and a lack of financial planning can keep high earners stuck on a hamster wheel , always working but never feeling financially safe or satisfied. Difficult words: lifestyle creep (slowly spending more as your income rises), net worth (everything you own minus everything you owe), hamster wheel (a cycle where you keep working but don’t feel progress). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people in the US make over 200,000 dollars a year, but they still don’t feel rich. These people are called HENRYs, which means High Earners, Not Rich Yet. Even people who make 300,000 dollars a year have money problems and debt s. They make more money, but they also spend more. This is called lifestyle creep. They buy more food, rent expensive homes, and want to live like their friends. They don’t always save enough money. Living in cities like New York or Los Angeles costs more, too. Even with high pay, people feel like they must keep working all the time. Experts say it is important to make a budget and know your net worth, which is what you own minus what you owe . That helps people plan and save for the future. Difficult words: debt (money you owe and must pay back), budget (a plan for how to spend money), owe (when you must give back something someone gave you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some Americans make a lot of money, but they do not feel rich . They are called HENRYs. This means High Earners, Not Rich Yet. Even people who make 300,000 dollars a year can have problems with money. They earn more, but they spend more too. This is called lifestyle creep. They spend more on food, rent, and fun. They also feel that they must have the same things as their friends. Many rich people live in big cities where everything is more expensive. Experts say that people should make a plan and save money. They need to know how much money they have and how much they owe . It helps them feel better about money and the future. Difficult words: rich (when you have a lot of money), earn (to get money for work), owe (when you must give back what you have from someone else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The growth of AI data centers in Georgia has caused a massive increase in electricity demand. To meet this need, the state’s main utility company is rapidly expanding its high-voltage power lines. The company’s 10-year infrastructure plan recently ballooned from just 24 miles of new lines to over 1,000 miles. 80 percent of this new energy will power data centers. However, this expansion is causing severe problems for local homeowners in towns like Fayetteville. New transmission lines are being built directly through private backyards, which requires hundreds of trees to be cut down. Residents argue that these massive structures destroy their property value, ruin their landscapes, and make it impossible to resell their homes at fair prices. While Georgia Power claims it offers fair compensation, many families feel forced into settlements because the company can use eminent domain to seize private land without the owners’ consent. Difficult words: utility company (a business that provides everyday public services like electricity, water, gas, or trash collection to a community), high-voltage (carrying a very large, powerful, and dangerous amount of electricity through wires over long distances), balloon (to suddenly grow, swell, or increase very quickly in size, number, or amount), eminent domain (a special legal rule that allows the government or a power company to take private land for public use, even if the owner says no). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many new computer data centers are opening in the state of Georgia. These centers need a very big amount of electricity to work. Because of this, the local power company is building more than 1,000 miles of new electrical lines. Most of this new energy will go directly to these big companies. But the companies are building power lines through the backyards of ordinary families. Workers are cutting down hundreds of trees, which ruins the beautiful view. Local homeowners are very angry because their houses are losing a lot of value , and they cannot sell them. The power company offers money to the families, but they say it is not enough to buy a new house. Homeowners feel they have no power to stop the company because the law allows the company to take private land. Difficult words: ordinary (normal), value (how much money somebody would pay to buy something), private (when something belongs to one person or family). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many new big data centers are opening in Georgia. These buildings need a lot of power. So, a big company is making many new power lines. These long lines go through the backyards of normal homes. Workers cut down many trees, and the yards look bad now. People are very sad and angry. They say that their houses cost less now, and they cannot sell them. The company gives some money to the people, but the parents say it is not enough to move away. The law says the company can take the land even if the people say no. Difficult words: data center (a large building with thousands of computers), line (a long, thin piece of metal which carries electricity), backyard (an area of land or a garden behind a house). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tourists visiting Athens are marveling at the Parthenon’s western pediment after restorers finally unveiled the ancient landmark. The temple is now visible in its most complete form in over 200 years. For a long time, the iconic structure on top of the Acropolis was covered by heavy construction equipment, large metal frames, and scaffolding , which blocked the view for visitors. Now, with all the building materials finally removed, people can see the ancient monument from both close up and further away without any visual obstacles . Visitors describe the newly uncovered temple as incredibly beautiful, special, and amazing. The complete view gives them a rare chance to see a little bit of how the historic building actually looked in the past. For many international travelers, seeing the clean, completed Acropolis fulfills a lifelong dream, with some even saying the majestic atmosphere makes it feel as though gods still live inside the building. Difficult words: pediment (a large triangular part of a building in ancient Greek style, usually found above the entrance or columns), scaffolding (a temporary structure made of metal pipes and wooden boards for workers to stand on while fixing a building), obstacles (an object or a thing that is in your way and blocks you from moving forward or seeing something), majestic (very big, beautiful, and powerful in a way that makes people feel great respect). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The famous Parthenon in Greece is finally finished after a long restoration . Restorers took away all the construction tools, metal frames, and scaffolding from the western side. Now, people can see the temple in its most complete form in over 200 years. Many tourists are very excited and happy about this change. Visitors who came last year remember a lot of building work, which blocked the beautiful view. Now, the temple is clean and open. People can look at it from close by or from far away. Travelers say the Acropolis looks amazing and very beautiful without the construction things in front of it. It helps them imagine how the great building looked like a long time ago. Difficult words: restoration (repairing an old building, painting, or object), scaffolding (a structure which workers use to repair a building), temple (a special building where people go to show respect to their god or gods). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Workers in Greece finish repairing the famous Parthenon temple . They take away all the metal construction. Now, the old building is open and clean. It is in its most complete form in over 200 years. Tourists from all over the world come to see it. Many people say that it is a big dream to see the Acropolis without the construction. Last year, there is too much construction. Now, the temple looks very beautiful and amazing. Visitors can see the building as in a long time ago. They can look at it from far away, or they can come close to it. Difficult words: repair (to fix something broken), temple (a special building where people go to show respect to their god or gods), complete (finished, with all the parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Parliament has approved new measures aimed at increasing the deportation of undocumented people. This sparked a heated confrontation among lawmakers. An alliance of centre-right and far-right politicians voted 418 to 218 in favor of the overhaul . Following the vote, right-wing lawmakers celebrated by jumping to their feet, pumping their fists, and chanting ‚send them back‘. In response, leftwing and centre-left politicians shouted back ‚shame on you‘, which showed deep political divisions . Human rights groups and UN experts have strongly criticized the plan and called it cruel and discriminatory . The new rules allow for people to be detained for up to two years or sent to offshore centres, which critics call human rights black holes. While far-right leaders welcomed the vote as a successful show of political force, opponents warned of hatred and damage to democratic institutions. They marked it a dark moment in European history. Difficult words: alliance (a group of people, political parties, or countries that agree to work together to achieve something), overhaul (a complete change to a system or a law to fix it or make it work in a brand new way), division (a deep and serious disagreement between two groups of people that separates them), discriminatory (unfair because it treats a specific group of people worse than others based on who they are). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The European leaders voted to approve a new law to increase sending illegal immigrants away. The vote passed with 418 politicians in favor and 218 against. After the vote, right-wing politicians celebrated and shouted ‚send them back‘ inside the government building. This made left-wing politicians very angry, and they shouted back ,shame on you.‘ The event showed that European leaders don’t agree on immigration. Some groups and experts strongly criticize the new rules. They say the plan is cruel because it allows the government to lock up people for two years or send them to faraway centers. Right-wing leaders are happy and say they are showing their power. Other politicians say this reaction is bad and makes people hate each other more. Difficult words: approve (to accept a plan, law, or idea officially), in favor (to support or agree with an idea or law in a vote), cruel (very unkind and hurting others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Leaders in Europe vote on a new law. They want to send illegal immigrants out of their countries. Many people in the government vote for the law. They are very happy. They stand up and shout. Other people are angry. This shows that the leaders have very different ideas. Many groups say that the new law is bad and unkind . It allows the government to put people in prison for two years. Some leaders say that this day is a dark time in the history of Europe. They think that the new rules will hurt families and children. Difficult words: immigrant (a person who comes to live in another country), government (people who control a country), unkind (not nice to other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US President Donald Trump has announced that Washington reached a historic peace agreement with Iran, mediated by Pakistan and Qatar. The deal includes an immediate and permanent end to military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon. According to Trump, Iran committed not to develop nuclear weapons and agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for global energy supplies. While the US might lift economic sanctions, Trump ruled out giving Tehran cash. Although a virtual signing was originally planned, it was delayed after Israel tried to disrupt the process. Pakistani Prime Minister announced that the official signing ceremony would now take place on Friday in Switzerland. If signed, the memorandum of understanding will start a 60-day negotiation period to solve the hardest problems, such as Iran’s enriched uranium stockpiles and its civilian nuclear programme, despite deep mistrust between both sides. Difficult words: mediate (to help two people or countries talk to each other so they can stop fighting and find an agreement), rule out (to decide that something is completely impossible or that you will definitely not allow it to happen), memorandum (an official written document or a short agreement that records a plan or a promise between people or governments). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The United States and Iran agreed on a new peace deal . Pakistan and Qatar helped both countries talk to each other. According to US President Donald Trump, Iran promises not to make nuclear weapons. They will also reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a very important sea route for oil. In return, America may stop its economic sanctions against Iran. The deal also stops all military fighting, including in Lebanon. At first, Trump wanted to sign the papers online immediately, but the plan changed. The Pakistani Prime Minister said the official signing ceremony will happen on Friday in Switzerland. If they sign the deal, they will have 60 days to discuss bigger problems about Iran’s nuclear projects. Difficult words: peace deal (an official agreement between countries to stop fighting a war), route (a path or road which people use to move things from one place to another), sanction (a ban which countries put on another country to stop them from trading or buying things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US and Iran have a new peace deal . Leaders from Pakistan and Qatar help them make this deal. The US President, Donald Trump, says that Iran will not make nuclear bombs. Iran will also open the Strait of Hormuz again. It is an important sea route for oil. This deal stops all fighting in the area. Trump wanted to sign the papers online, but it does not happen. Now, the official ceremony will be on Friday in Switzerland. If they sign the papers, they will have 60 days to talk about bigger problems. Many people are happy about this peace. Difficult words: peace deal (an official deal which stops a war or fighting), route (a path or road which people use to move things from one place to another), ceremony (a formal event). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
